clue.text: Brief Kipling novel carried by Observer

indicators.note: what is carried sits inside its carrier, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a spy is someone who secretly observes
Kim is Rudyard Kipling's 1901 novel

explanation.surface: A short Kipling novel being serialised in The Observer newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The italics make Observer look like the newspaper; here it is simply a watcher, someone who keeps an eye on others.
explanation.definitionFit: Something skimpy is scanty or minimal, like a brief garment, so the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Ignore American bum getting upset

indicators.note: to upset something is to overturn it, so in a down clue the letters are turned bottom to top

parts.note: buns is US slang for the buttocks

explanation.surface: Someone advised to ignore an American layabout who is getting upset.
explanation.walkthrough: Bum here is the backside, not a tramp, and the American word for it is BUNS.
explanation.definitionFit: To snub someone is to rebuff or pointedly disregard them, a close synonym of ignoring.

clue.text: In communications, I omitted article from US state

indicators.note: something omitted is left out, so letters are dropped from the longer word

parts.note: Indiana is a Midwestern US state
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A writer admits to leaving an article out of their communications about a US state.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition hides at the start: in radio communications, the letter I is spoken as INDIA. Removing AN from INDIANA leaves it.
explanation.definitionFit: The NATO phonetic alphabet used in radio signalling gives the code word India for the letter I.

clue.text: Old man with failing clarity is very drunk

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: something failing is breaking down, so the letters collapse into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An elderly father whose clear thinking is slipping turns out to be thoroughly drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Paralytic is British slang for extremely drunk, unable to stand.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, being paralytic means so intoxicated you can barely move, an informal synonym.

clue.text: Man's man is connecting with a punch

parts.note: taken as written
one who lands a punch connects with it

explanation.surface: One man is landing a blow on another.
explanation.walkthrough: Man is the Isle of Man, the self-governing island in the Irish Sea, so a Man's man is someone who lives there.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhabitant of the Isle of Man is an islander, a resident of an island.

clue.text: Jazz piece (American) put up before exclusive item from The Nutcracker?

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something up raises it so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a rag is a piece of ragtime music
US is short for American
a plum job or role is a highly sought-after one

explanation.surface: A jazz number staged ahead of a prestige excerpt from Tchaikovsky's ballet.
explanation.walkthrough: The Nutcracker features the Dance of the Sugar Plum Fairy; the question mark flags that the item is only part of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sugar Plum Fairy is a famous character in Tchaikovsky's ballet, with her own celebrated dance.

clue.text: Prank not in support of clubs

parts.note: anti means opposed
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A prank pulled by someone who does not back the golf or nightclubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Antic is usually met in the plural, but the singular noun is a playful trick.
explanation.definitionFit: An antic is a grotesque or playful caper, much the same thing as a practical joke.

clue.text: Study: no repeated sexual intercourse boosted the arrival of nippers?

parts.note: a den is a study, a private room for work

indicators.note: boosting lifts something upward, which in a down clue sends the letters bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
IT is slang for sex, and repeated makes it appear twice

explanation.surface: Research finding that abstinence led to a baby boom, which sounds contradictory.
explanation.walkthrough: Nippers looks like children, but here they are teeth, which nip.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentition means the cutting of teeth, so the arrival of things that bite is a playful paraphrase.

clue.text: Grub and drink, German, in stock

parts.note: to grub is to dig or root about
gin is a spirit
Ger. is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: Food and a German drink are kept in stock in the pantry.
explanation.walkthrough: Grub looks like food but is the verb to dig. A stock or rootstock is the underground stem of a plant, which is what root ginger is.
explanation.definitionFit: Root ginger is the knobbly rhizome of the ginger plant, botanically a rootstock, sold whole for cooking.

clue.text: Daughter taking time to engage in shrewd exercises? It's a product of breeding

indicators.note: to engage in is to become involved inside something, so one piece enters another

parts.note: wily means cunning or shrewd
PE is physical education, school exercises
D is the abbreviation for daughter
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A daughter makes time for clever workouts, a trait apparently inherited.
explanation.walkthrough: The daughter and time travel together as a pair before going in. In genetics the wild type is the normal, naturally occurring form of an organism, as opposed to a mutant.
explanation.definitionFit: Geneticists call the strain found in natural breeding populations the wild type, contrasted with mutant strains.

clue.text: Stress not entirely shown by good junior worker

indicators.note: not entirely means incomplete, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to underline a point is to stress it
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A junior employee shows signs of not being completely stressed out.
explanation.walkthrough: Stress is the verb to emphasise, not the feeling of strain.
explanation.definitionFit: An underling is a subordinate, someone low in an organisation's hierarchy, often used disparagingly.

clue.text: The way to embrace no good dance

indicators.note: an embrace wraps arms around someone, so one piece holds another

parts.note: the Tao is the Way in Chinese philosophy
NG is the abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: Advice that the way to hold a partner is not a good dance move.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tao, meaning the way, is the guiding principle of Taoism.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is a ballroom dance originating in Argentina, so it is an example of a dance.

clue.text: Everyone will participate in rotten song

indicators.note: to participate is to take part within something, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: rotten means bad
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A singalong where everyone joins in with a terrible song.
explanation.walkthrough: Will participate in sounds like a crowd joining a chorus; it simply places one word inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballad is a narrative poem set to music or a slow sentimental popular number, a kind of song.

clue.text: Urging sleep or dancing the night away?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: swaying a cradle gently to lull a baby
second meaning: dancing energetically to rock music

explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings sound like opposite evenings, one quiet and one wild, yet the same word covers both.
explanation.definitionFit: Swaying an infant back and forth to send it off, and moving to loud music, are both described by this participle.

clue.text: Mild in East, producing fruit

parts.note: clement weather is mild
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: Mild weather in the East lets trees bear fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Clement is most often used of weather, meaning gentle and mild.
explanation.definitionFit: A clementine is a small sweet citrus, a cross between a mandarin and an orange.

clue.text: Minor plague seeing off British

indicators.note: to see someone off is to make them leave, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a blight is a plague or affliction
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A small-scale epidemic that drives away the British.
explanation.walkthrough: BLIGHT without its B leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Light and minor both describe something of little weight or seriousness, as in a light offence.

clue.text: A grub spot, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so the letters may be reordered

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A place where one might get some food, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the letters to rearrange and the definition: a gastropub is literally a spot for grub.
explanation.definitionFit: A gastropub is a pub specialising in good food, so it is indeed a place to eat.

clue.text: Contamination: positive outcome eradicating sulphur, bringing in touch of life

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for positive

indicators.note: bringing something in places it inside, so a letter is inserted
eradicating wipes something out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a solution is the outcome of a problem
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

indicators.note: a touch is just a small amount, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A report on contamination: a good result after removing sulphur and introducing living organisms.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove S from SOLUTION, slip L into what remains, and put P in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Pollution is the introduction of harmful substances into the environment, which is contamination.

clue.text: To relinquish Government control of tax is blocked by a lot of peers? On the contrary

indicators.note: something blocked is hemmed in, so one piece is held inside another
this phrase flips the instruction just given, so the holder and the held swap roles
a lot of means most but not all, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to peer is to look closely, as one who pries
VAT is value added tax, a British sales tax
taken as written

explanation.surface: A plan to end state control of taxation is thwarted by the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: Peers looks like members of the Lords, but it is the verb meaning looks closely. On the contrary means the tax goes inside the shortened peers, not the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: To privatise is to transfer an industry or service from state ownership into private hands.

clue.text: Ready to fight in damp regions on hot days?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, as two words: equipped with weapons for battle
second meaning: the armpits, which sweat in the heat

explanation.walkthrough: The same letters read as a phrase about soldiers and as a body part; the question mark admits the comic second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops under arms are mobilised for battle, and armpits are the sweatiest part of the body in summer.

clue.text: Chap's put in misplaced commas, relishing the discomfort caused

indicators.note: putting something in places it inside, so one piece goes within another
things misplaced are out of their proper order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
his is the possessive of a male chap

explanation.surface: A man takes pleasure in the pain he causes by putting commas in the wrong places.
explanation.walkthrough: Chap's stands for the possessive pronoun HIS, which is placed inside the rearranged COMMAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Masochism is the tendency to take pleasure in one's own pain or suffering.

clue.text: Slow learner caught getting stuck into SF blockbuster

indicators.note: something stuck into another is lodged inside it

parts.note: Dune is a science-fiction film based on Frank Herbert's novel
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A dim pupil found engrossed in a sci-fi epic.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes inside DUNE.
explanation.definitionFit: A dunce is a person slow at learning, traditionally the dullest pupil in the class.

clue.text: Rock group turned popular with artist covering lead position

indicators.note: something turned faces the other way, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: a cover wraps around something, so one piece goes outside another

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
the van is the front, the leading position

explanation.surface: A rock band became popular, with a painter taking the frontman's role.
explanation.walkthrough: Lead position is the vanguard, the front of an army. Nirvana was the Seattle grunge band fronted by Kurt Cobain.
explanation.definitionFit: Nirvana was a hugely successful American rock band of the early 1990s.

clue.text: A long time to induct new saint

indicators.note: inducting someone admits them inside an organisation

parts.note: ages means a long time
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Canonising a new saint takes a very long time.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes inside AGES. St Agnes is an early Roman virgin martyr.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnes of Rome is a well-known early Christian martyr venerated as a saint.

clue.text: Appreciate routine may turn overblown?

indicators.note: turning something round sends it back the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to dig something is slang for appreciating it
a rut is a dull routine

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a valued routine might become inflated and pompous.
explanation.walkthrough: Dig is the slang verb for liking something.
explanation.definitionFit: Turgid prose is swollen and pompous, so it is bombastic and inflated in style.

clue.text: See 9
Henry appearing under flag of European country

parts.note: a flag is a type of iris plant
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A man called Henry pictured beneath a European nation's flag.
explanation.walkthrough: Flag looks like a national banner but is the yellow iris; in a down clue, H appearing under it comes after.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish is the adjective for things relating to Ireland, a nation in western Europe.

clue.text: The soul of Italy, to be found in carnal matters?

indicators.note: something found in a phrase is located inside its run of letters

parts.note: the letters run across the join between the two words

explanation.surface: A wry suggestion that Italy's spirit lies in matters of the flesh.
explanation.walkthrough: The soul of Italy means the Italian word for soul.
explanation.definitionFit: Alma is the Italian word for soul or spirit, so the definition asks for a foreign translation.

clue.text: Top score in playing pontoon or Newmarket for starters

indicators.note: starters come at the beginning, so each word gives its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letters of these five words

explanation.surface: The best score in the card games pontoon or Newmarket.
explanation.walkthrough: Pontoon and Newmarket are British card games, which steers you toward cards, but the answer is the full-point win in judo.
explanation.definitionFit: In judo, an ippon is the highest score, a full point that wins the bout outright.

clue.text: Communicate to pupil about one area without prejudice

parts.note: to impart information is to communicate it
I is the Roman numeral one
A is the abbreviation for area
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A teacher tells a pupil about a topic with no bias.
explanation.walkthrough: About here means next to: I and A sit beside L at the end, after IMPART.
explanation.definitionFit: Being impartial means treating all sides equally, showing no bias or favouritism.

clue.text: Uncovered countermeasure to restrain manager with relief

indicators.note: restraining something holds it in, so one piece encloses another
uncovered means stripped of its outer layer, so the end letters go

parts.note: a remedy counters a problem
a boss is a manager

explanation.surface: Holding a manager back with a countermeasure brought relief.
explanation.walkthrough: Relief looks like comfort, but it is a design raised from a surface. Uncovered strips the first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An embossed surface carries a raised design, which is what art calls being in relief.

clue.text: Complexity in maths leading to a complaint

indicators.note: complexity implies tangled parts, so the letters are knotted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: A student finds difficult mathematics provokes a grumble.
explanation.walkthrough: Complaint looks like a grumble, but here it is an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Asthma is a chronic respiratory condition, and a complaint is an ailment or illness.
